Theorem
[Existence and uniqueness on a noncompact manifold, evolving metric] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0323, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0324 ↗ thm:chow-iii-evolving-dirichlet-heat-kernel ↗ lem:chow-iii-dirichlet-kernel-mass-bound 1. ch24:24.40\group Noncompact Heat Kernels

Let $\mathcal M$ be noncompact, let $g(\tau )$ be a smooth family of metrics, and suppose $Q$ is uniformly bounded. Then $L_{x,\tau }$ has a unique smooth minimal positive fundamental solution $H_{\mathcal M}(x,\tau ;y,v)$.
Proof

\sketch For an exhaustion $\Omega _i\Subset \Omega _{i+1}$, the maximum principle gives $0<H_{\Omega _i}\le H_{\Omega _{i+1}}$. The mass bound below and a local parabolic mean-value inequality make the monotone limit finite on compact subsets; local derivative estimates make it smooth. It has the delta initial condition and is dominated by every positive fundamental solution, proving minimality and uniqueness.

□
